messages.author: af3457675e3c4ce8
messages.subject: Reinforcement Learning with 3 trial types
parts:
Hi there,

I don't have much experience in computational modeling, so bear with me for non-technical description of my issues!

I'm using a reinforcement learning task that should be the bandit2arm task. Participants need to choose 1 of the 2 options with different outcomes. However, this task has 3 types of trials: Reward trials (win vs. non-win), Punishment trials (avoid losing vs. losing), and Neutral trials (no winning or losing either choice). Therefore, participants see 6 stimuli (in 3 pairs in total). Each pair of stimuli is corresponding to one trial type.

From my understanding of the hBayesDM package, there doesn't seem to be a model that codes outcome 1, 0, and -1 at the same time, is there? I would need to calculate the expected values and prediction errors as the model regressors for fMRI analysis, therefore, although the Q-learning model seems to have more stimuli types (up to 6), it doesn't calculate model regressors.

If my understanding of the package is correct, how can we deal with this? Can we run a separate model estimation for each condition (e.g. fitting the prl_rp model 3 times to reward, neutral, and punishment trials)? If that's the case, should I differentiate in the Outcome column by using 1, 0, and -1? Or it's okay to use 1 as winning/avoid losing, and -1 as no-win and losing money?

Thanks in advance for viewing my questions. Looking forward to hearing from you.

Regards,
Cynthia

messages.author: af3457675e3c4ce8
messages.subject: RE: Reinforcement Learning with 3 trial types
parts:
Hi Lei,

 

Thank you for directing me to the post! I also came across this post about coding non-rewarded outcomes as 0 instead of -1: https://groups.google.com/u/1/g/hbayesdm-users/c/5rQwyiBdCEs

 

If I’m separating 3 trial types and do separate model parameter estimations for them, should I code differently for 3 trial types? For example,

Reward trials: win (1), non-win (0)

Punishment trials: non-loss (0), loss (-1)

 

But it then becomes a problem for neutral trials. In neutral trials, 2 outcomes are both neutral (0). But people sometimes grew a preference for one of the two. We would like to tease that piece out. Would it make sense that we always use 1 and -1 for 3 runs of the model? In other words, win, non-loss, and one of the neutral outcome will be 1, and non-win, loss, and the other neutral outcome will be -1, in their respective models.

 

Thanks again for your help!

 

Regards,

Cynthia
